newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gilts seek support at 113-29.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gilts seek support at 113-29.

text.p: September gilts will struggle to break 115-00 on Thursday, but barring any surprises from the Bank of England on interest rates later, support just below 114-00 should hold, technical analysts said.
"On the gilt we've run into quite serious trouble at 115-00," said Elli Gifford, an independent technical analyst based near Cambridge.
"There's little sign of even an attempt to take that out and I suspect we'll come back to around 114-00."
Gifford put a fairly solid band of support at 113-29 to 113-24.
Charts show the market hit a low of 113-24 on July 3, 113-25 on July 2, 113-26 on June 30 and 113-29 on July 1.
"The selling pressure is slackening so that support should hold," said Gifford.
By 0705 GMT September gilts were down 3/32 at 114-06.
The Bank of England is due to announce the outcome of its monetary policy meeting around 1100 GMT. Most economists expect a 25 basis point interest rate rise.
"The market's taken a view and if they (the Bank of England) do nothing, or something more than expected, the market will move and move fast," said Gifford.
Hans-Guenter Redeker, technical analyst at Chase, said as long as the market remained below 114-17, it would put 114-06 under pressure.
"Once below here, it will decline to 113-24, the low traded on July 7," Redeker said in a note for clients.
He said a move below 113-24 suggested a test of trend line support at 113-14. "A daily closing price below here allows a move to 113-06."
To the upside, Redeker said a move above 114-27 suggested a break of the 115-05 contract high made on July 2. "If above here, it will test trendline resistance at 115-17," he said.
By 0730 GMT, December short sterling was up one basis point at 92.56.
